metadata.scope: Xu-style Najia (徐氏納甲法) day-stem/hour-branch point-opening tables: open channel, five-shu/original point identity, open/closed (閉穴) state. Historical procedural citation only; never treatment instruction.
not_scope: Linggui Bafa (靈龜八法) / Feiteng Bafa (飛騰八法)
Yangzi shike zhuxue fa (養子時刻注穴法)
any procedural or clinical content whatsoever (needling, pressure, moxibustion)

primary_source.work_title: Zhenjiu Dacheng (針灸大成), Yang Jizhou 楊繼洲
primary_source.volume_or_chapter: 卷七 (see edition_note: some scans paginate this corpus as 第五卷)

cross_reference_source.role: originating-work collation (the Dacheng corpus reproduces Xu Feng's tables); resolves dropped glyphs and records edition variants

metadata.edition_note: The research note's 'vol. 5' follows the shidianguiji scan (book NA08718), unreachable at freeze time (re-checked 2026-09-04). The reachable Wikisource edition of 針灸大成 arranges the 徐氏 corpus in 卷七; CTEXT 針灸大全 prints the same corpus in 卷之五. Gate 1 confirms the final edition_or_facsimile_uri and the volume arrangement.
collation_notes: 榮 (freeze edition, 針灸大成卷七) vs 滎 (針灸大全卷之五) for the ying point class: same point class, edition orthography.
邱墟 (freeze edition) vs 丘墟 (針灸大全): same point, edition orthography.
沖 vs 衝 graph variance across sections and editions (太沖/太衝, 中沖/中衝, 關沖, 衝陽): recorded per row from the verse form; Gate 1 confirms against facsimile.
戊日 verse: Wikisource drops one graph before 「陽土穴必還原」; 針灸大全 prints 「衝陽土穴必還原」 — restored as 衝陽.
丁日 verse: 「發丑復溜」 (Wikisource) vs 「癸丑複溜」 (CTEXT) — restored as 癸丑復溜.
辛日 verse: Wikisource drops the second graph of 「太[ ]原太淵」; CTEXT prints 「乙未太衝原太淵」 — restored as 太衝; the 流注圖 transcribes the slot as 「己未時」, collated to 乙未.
壬日 verse: Wikisource prints 「大腸庚戍曲池真」 (戍) — collated to 庚戌 from the 流注圖 「庚戌時 大腸合土」.
壬日 table: the 針灸大全 verse omits the 戊申/庚戌/壬子 rows; 針灸大成 verse and 流注圖 include them. Freeze follows 針灸大成; the omission is recorded as an edition variant, not merged.
癸日 己巳: Wikisource 「己已商邱」 — collated to 己巳.
乙日 乙未: 針灸大成 「乙未勞宮火穴榮」 with 流注圖 「血納包絡之榮火」; 針灸大全 prints 「水穴滎」 — freeze follows 火 (figure and doctrine: 木生火).
癸日 closing figure prints 「癸木屬水，謂水生木也」 — quoted as printed; doctrine reads 癸 as water generating the 井木 point 中沖.

resolution_conventions.hour_branch_windows: Amlich local civil hour-branch slots, unchanged: 子 23:00–01:00, 丑 01:00–03:00, … , 亥 21:00–23:00 (reuse of resolve_hour_branch_slot contract; boundary tests at 22:59/23:00/00:59/01:00).
resolution_conventions.day_attribution_rule: The 23:00–01:00 子 block belongs to the civil date containing its 00:00–01:00 half (classical 子-opens-the-day attribution). For 01:00–23:00 the cell day stem is the current civil date's day stem. Pinned per TNLC-DIV-03; engine goldens freeze the 甲→乙 and a yin-pair 亥/子 boundaries.
resolution_conventions.hour_pillar_rule: 五鼠遁 from the cell day stem (甲己日起甲子), matching Amlich compute_hour_pillar seed mapping.
resolution_conventions.open_rule: Cell (day stem d, hour branch h) is open iff its hour pillar equals a row pillar of a day-table whose running window covers that cell; own-day table rows and previous-day-table spillover rows tile the cycle continuously. All other cells are closed (閉穴). Cross-day spillover is inherent: every table except 甲 opens on its opening day and its last rows land on the next civil day; the 壬-table's closing 壬子 row lands on the 癸 day's 子 block.
resolution_conventions.duplicate_pillar_rule: Twelve hour pillars appear in two tables (甲↔庚: 庚辰/壬午/甲申; 乙↔辛: 辛卯/癸巳/乙未; 丙↔壬: 壬寅/甲辰/丙午; 己↔癸: 己巳/辛未/癸酉). Each resolves uniquely by cell day stem via the window rule; no interpolation.

disclaimer_v2_draft.vi: Trích dẫn thuật ngữ y học cổ truyền từ văn bản Châm Cứu Đại Thành; chỉ mang tính văn hóa – lịch sử. Đây không phải hướng dẫn châm, bấm, cứu hay tự điều trị tại bất kỳ thời điểm nào. Không dùng để trì hoãn hoặc thay thế chăm sóc từ nhân viên y tế có chuyên môn.
disclaimer_v2_draft.en: Citations of classical acupuncture terminology from Zhenjiu Dacheng; provided as historical and cultural information only. This is not instruction or encouragement to needle, press, moxibust, or self-treat at any time. Do not use it to delay or replace care from a qualified health professional.
